I don't know if this has already been mentioned, but I felt like this might be useful advice. And I've seen issues that could probably be remedied by this method in many of the deepfakes released.

Faces of different sizes will have different optimal blur and kernel sizes. So if you have a clip in which there are multiple zoom levels, using the same merge settigns for all of them will result in some faces being blurred (and eroded) either too much or too little.

So instead, sort the frames according to face size, and merge them one batch at a time with different settings.

This allows you get more consistently blended edges.

The cross section (interaction) between the alpha particles and the electrons of the foil is negligible, so all the alpha particles see are the gold nuclei. I guess I understand less than I thought, maybe a more general question would be better:

How does quantum tunneling work?

Well, in quantum mechanics, the wave function determines how much a particle is present in different locations. High (absolute) value of the wave function somewhere means that the particle is mostly in that location. The wave function is continuous, so if it reaches a barrier it has two possibilities: it has to be exactly zero at the barrier, or it "leaks" through the barrier. This happens whether the barrier is of lower energy than the energy of the particle, or higher energy. If the barrier is not too high in energy and not too thick, you can find a non-negligible remainder of the wave function on the other side. If you then cause a collapse, the particle can end up completely on the other side of the barrier, even if it classically did not have enough energy to cross it.

Barriers of infinite height force the wave function to be zero at the barrier and allow no tunneling whatsoever.
